newsitem.title: UK: U.S. stocks in London mostly firmer, techs bounce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks in London mostly firmer, techs bounce.

text.p: U.S. shares trading in London were generally firmer on Tuesday as technology stocks bounced after a slide on Wall Street but tobacco stocks stumbled, dealers said.
Firmer long bond and S&P 500 futures pointed to a steady to higher open in New York, they said. "All the play has been in the high-techs. There's a bounce going on in the techs," one dealer said.

"In the rest of the market, technically there are a few buyers around. Bonds showed some improvement this morning and futures look OK, so a lot of people are going for a steadier opening on Wall Street," he added.

But the dealer said currency concerns could continue to weigh on U.S. shares. "There's been talk about how the dollar's hurting stocks with big overseas exposure, which is what brought IBM crashing off yesterday," he said.
By 1140 GMT in London, IBM was up $1/2 at $143-1/4 while Intel Corp gained $7/8 to $152-1/2 and Digital Equipment Corp rose $1/4 to $34-1/2.
But tobacco shares weakened as worries about litigation continued to weigh, dealers said. Philip Morris was down $3/8 at $119-7/8 and RJR Nabisco was $1/8 lower at $33-7/8.
March S&P 500 futures trading on Globex were 1.20 points firmer at 789.25 and the March long bond future was up 3/32 at 112-18/32.
